Lakemont will reopen its flooded central library as a larger, late-opening community hub. Almost everyone in town welcomes it; a few ask about the cost.

On Thursday the "Lakemont Town Council" approved a plan to rebuild the "Lakemont Central Library", closed since last spring's flood, and to open it until 10 pm on weekdays. "Harriet Vance", the town librarian, said the new building will add a children's floor, a job-seekers' room and free study space for students. "Owen Park", chair of the council's finance committee, said a state resilience grant covers most of the cost.

"Beatrice Lin", president of the "Lakemont Parents Network", said families have waited a year and the children's floor is "the best news this town has had". "Samuel Reyes", head teacher at "Lakemont High School", said students will finally have a quiet place to study after school. "Grace Fulton", who leads the "Lakemont Seniors Club", said members are delighted that the reading room will return with larger print books.

"Victor Hale" of the "Lakemont Small Business Circle" said shops near the library expect more evening visitors. "Aisha Rahman", a volunteer at the "Lakemont Food Bank", said the job-seekers' room will help families her group supports. "Dr. Colin Marsh", who studies public libraries at "Lakemont Community College", said late opening hours have raised visits by a quarter in similar towns.

"Peter Quill", a retired accountant who writes a column for the "Lakemont Gazette", asked the council to publish the maintenance budget before building starts. The "Lakemont Gazette" said the first phase will open next autumn.
